gates.name: The ROI gate (LOC-11)
gates.rule: Reopen or keep a language only when both hold. Demand: in-language search volume for the anchor tasks, or for the niche queries this domain wins, of the order of the English page's own traffic from that country, on Trends and visible as in-language queries in GSC. Field: an English page of ours already ranks in the top ten on the same kind of query, showing the domain can compete in that field before a native edition asks it to.

gates.name: Translated-results reading
gates.rule: On a language Google's translated-results feature covers, a machine-translated incumbent is a sign of thin native demand, not an opening: the translator is Google, applied to the whole English field, so a native page would compete with Google's translation of the majors. Such a language needs a stronger case on both halves of the gate.

gates.name: Review and freshness gate
gates.rule: A localized tool page or guide publishes only with reviewer, reviewedAt, reviewNotes and a sourceHash that matches the English source; an English edit to a translated page fails the build until the translation is re-reviewed. The home edition is the recorded exception: it published as a disclosed AI draft pending Shlomi's own read-through.

gates.name: The original pilot rule (LOC-01), superseded in emphasis
gates.rule: A language went to a pilot when native phrasing carried a comparable share to English on two of four anchor tasks, at least one incumbent on the top phrasing was mixed-language or machine-translated, and a native reviewer was available. Written before the data. Indonesian met the first and third and was still held, which is what produced the ROI gate.

mechanism: A locale is a prefixed route family on the one origin: /he/ (home), /he/<tool>/ and /he/<guide>/, each a content-collection entry that overlays translated fields on the English source (src/i18n/, src/content/localized-*). One origin keeps drafts, IndexedDB and the service worker shared.

Tool islands take a server-rendered messages catalogue (src/i18n/toolMessages.ts); the shared shell (dropzone, file row, confirmations, app bar, footer) has its own. The Sign and Redact editor stays English behind a disclosed notice, as does the home page's interactive demo.

RTL is a layout property: logical CSS plus dir on the page; the app bar's arrows and the demo's captions mirror. A language-purity check (scripts/localizedSeoChecks.mjs) scores each localized page's visible text and excludes only the disclosed-English islands.

Every edition carries reciprocal hreflang with x-default, its own sitemap entries, and an offline pack the page asks the service worker to warm. Search Console reads per locale start at the 2026-10-08 refresh (findings doc § 3.7).

Evidence for a decision lives in its LOC ticket under backlog/tasks/; this page holds the verdict, the numbers that carried it, and the date it comes back. Edit here, publish, and sync docs/i18n-status/data/i18n-status.json in the repo.

languages.name: Hebrew
languages.reasoning: Chosen first because review costs nothing (in-house), Israel already converts best of any country from English queries, and the Hebrew incumbents are visibly weak: machine-flavoured, LTR-laid-out, none claiming on-device processing or real RTL support. LOC-01 called Hebrew's small Trends share "informative, not decisive" for exactly that reason. LOC-11 later confirmed Hebrew is one of the weakest demand cases measured; the decision stands because the marginal cost is zero.
languages.next: First read at the 2026-10-08 refresh (LOC-06's per-locale table); success criteria read at the eight-week mark, 2026-11-06: any Hebrew-query impression at all, or one of the three target phrasings in Israel's top 20. As of 2026-09-12 the home page's dock and cards are fully Hebrew and the Sign editor's toolbar row is a Hebrew draft, with the rest of the editor still English (LOC-09).

languages.name: Indonesian
languages.reasoning: Generic tool pages stay held, per LOC-07: "criterion 1 alone does not carry the decision... the one piece of direct evidence this domain has about ranking against this exact competitive field says it currently cannot, and a translation does not change that." Indonesian is also on Google's translated-results list. What LOC-14 found is narrower and cleared the ROI gate on its own: at 1 MB, Keyword Planner puts kompres pdf 1 mb at 50,000/month against the English pages' entire Indonesian footprint of 151 impressions a quarter, and Trends shows a steady native line at roughly 4% of generic kompres pdf, 12x English at that limit. The 100 to 300 KB family sits below Trends' floor. Field passes with a caveat: no Indonesian result claims on-device processing, but the field is the same second tier this domain already beats in English at 9.4.
languages.next: LOC-15: source a paid native reviewer, cite the real portal limits (SSCASN/BKN, SKCK, PPPK, SNPMB), build the one standalone page for under-1MB PDF and under-200KB photo, publish and request indexing. Read eight weeks after indexing on the kompres pdf 1 mb / di bawah 1 mb family in GSC Indonesia. The generic pages (retired LOC-04) reopen only if the Hebrew pilot produces measurable in-language impressions, or an English tool page reaches page one for its own head term.
